assumptions: primes <= 1e7 by sieve (664579 primes); gaps coded raw and halved (gap/2, first gap dropped)
posting lists: 1e5 geometric(0.001) gaps; bursty: 100 segments x 1000 gaps with p drawn from {0.1, 0.01, 0.001, 0.0001}
zeroth-order empirical entropy as reference (codes are memoryless)
falsification: Pattern codes never best among universal codes on these data.
hypothesis: On prime gaps (light tail, mean ~15) gamma-like codes or Fibonacci win; on bursty posting-list gaps (heavy-tailed mixture) pattern codes beat both classical universal codes and a tuned Golomb code; on homogeneous posting lists (geometric gaps) tuned Golomb wins.
methodology: Average bits per value for every code (exact, from the empirical distribution); tuned codes are tuned on the same data (optimistic for them).
question: Do the synthetic conclusions survive on concrete integer sequences?
